minutes.headline: Sewer Commission moved to deny a second lawn-watering credit unless the resident installs an irrigation meter
minutes.summary: The commission heard its first quarterly review from the sewer contractor, including a proposed pump station control upgrade. It also covered the Lunenburg Village 40B fee positions, the Lancaster Ave extension, grease trap compliance and the Fitchburg agreement. A sewer credit request was handled by motion, and the meeting calendar was adjusted.

votes.motion: Deny the sewer credit request, amended so the current invoice is credited if the resident installs an irrigation meter and shows proof by end of November

what_happened.line: The commission voted on a motion to deny a sewer credit request unless the resident installs an irrigation meter and shows proof by the end of November; the vote tally was not audible.
Staff and DPW were asked to review the contractor's control system estimate with the vendor and bring a recommendation back to the commission.
The commission recommended that only the originally waived privilege fee units stand, and that the 40B applicant pays the connection fee in effect at original filing.
A request to pay a betterment over a longer term than the bylaw allows was not granted; the collector will be told the term stays at 10 years.
The November meeting was moved to December 3, with December 17 tentative, and the commission will look at paying for the control system from the enterprise fund or project funds.

why_it_matters: Sewer credits for lawn watering now depend on proof of a separate irrigation meter, which affects any household that wants an abatement for outdoor water that does not enter the sewer.
Paying for the pump station control upgrade from the enterprise fund or project funds would put the cost on sewer users' rates or on project money, not the general tax levy.
